title: Visualisations
headline: Open the fish (/blueprint3d/) now runs on the other threads' real files where they exist: the gill lamella uses physiology/countercurrent.js (utilisation 56 % counter-current vs 40 % co-current on the stand-in parameters, effectiveness 71 % vs 50 %), the circulation particles beat at the heart rate of physiology/cardiac.js's proxy (schoolmaster snapper, 96 to 153 /min via an effort slider), and every piece's panel opens with the Lean grounding verdict from lean/morphology-grounding.json (pectoral fin: lifting area needed 0.012316 m² at 10 m/s against 0.012688 m² measured). genotype/interactions.json exists but holds no interaction yet, and the tissue and cell views say so with the file's own note. The Physics stage embeds the physics thread's flight simulator. Open the fish (/blueprint3d/) now has four modes: Anatomy (the 3D cutaway), Physiology (animated single-circuit blood flow over the model's organ centres, particles coloured by oxygenation, plus a gill-lamella zoom with water and blood flowing opposite ways, live PO2 profiles and a co-current toggle: counter-current extracts 57 % of the water's O2 and lets blood leave at 116 mmHg against 40 % and 90 mmHg co-current, on stand-in parameters), Tissue signalling and Cell-cell interactions (the fin's tissues, bud parts and post-composed cell types drawn as nodes; arrows styled solid for experimental and dashed for orthology-inferred evidence). Both physiology and interactions run on labelled stand-ins: physiology/ and genotype/interactions.json do not exist yet, every animation states on screen which values are flying-fish data (none), proxy-teleost or assumed, and the build copies the real files in when they land. 'Open the fish' at /blueprint3d/ is now a real 3D cutaway: the Blender-built segmented model (model/flying-fish.glb, 110 named pieces, driven by model/manifest.json) loads in three.js; a split slider swings the L/R halves apart, a peel slider hides skin, then muscle, then skeleton, leaving the organs; clicking any piece opens its ontology node (or says the blueprint has none and names the nearest ancestor) with the gene strip, the drill-down list, and a provenance panel that traces the term and query, explicit claim-graph edges, the Lean constraints that apply with their proof scope (C6 for every node; C8, C8c, C9, C12 for skeleton and fin, all marked as about the model, not the fish), the unsigned nanopub drafts that cite it, and the physics figures for the fin; the gene lens tints every piece a gene touches; the Wing genes preset and the Daane 2021 inset are kept. Only the pectoral fin length (0.687 of standard length) is evidence-backed; the canvas says the geometry is schematic. 'Open the fish' is now the default blueprint page at /blueprint3d/ (approved by Amit 2026-10-31; the radial 3D view stays at /blueprint3d/?view=radial): the genotype-phenotype map as a flying fish opened layer by layer: a schematic side view (drawn for the page, not anatomy), an explode slider for the 13 organ systems, organs fanning from a system, an x-ray of one organ with its tissues and cell-type chips, a ranked gene strip at every level (sufficient > required > expressed, proxy fish only), a gene lens that lights every node a gene touches (3119 genes), and a Wing genes preset that pins kcnk5b, kcnh2a and slc43a2a at the whole pectoral fin, draws the genotype thread's zebrafish fin subtree below it (50 ZFA terms, 5 zebrafish-only, precursor bud on a separate develops_from lane) and states that no wing gene has a record below the organ.  The flying-fish blueprint is drawn in 3D at /blueprint3d/ with its genes: 536 distinct ontology terms (13 organ systems, 67 organs, 198 tissues, 257 cell types), 674 part_of edges, and one gene marker on each of the 79 nodes that has a direct proxy-fish record in the vetted genotype map (genotype/map.vetted.slim.json, a committed source, so a clean checkout reproduces the page) (body 1/1, organ systems 8/13, organs 28/67, tissues 29/198, cell types 14/257); every gene section says the records were measured in zebrafish or medaka, never in a flying fish, and that a node with no record is unstudied, not gene-free. Each node also shows its term, the SPARQL query that produced it, and the kernel-checked structural certificate that covers it beside the biological Lean statement it does not have (0 of 536 terms appear in any Lean statement). /graph/ hides its 213 datasets by default and its Ideas view reads 12 ideas: 4 researched, 5 reach-synthesis (not yet checked against prior art), 3 serendipitous.
